chunks: And also what he narrated: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Uthman from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fasts a voluntary fast which he has fixed upon himself, or who fasts the sacred months, and the month or two months pass without him making it up. He said: He said, 'He does not fast during travel, nor does he make up anything from the voluntary fast except the three days that he used to fast in every month, and he does not make them equivalent to the obligatory fast, except that I love for you to persist in the good deed.'
He said, 'And for the one who fasts the sacred months, it suffices him to fast three days in place of each month of the sacred months.'

And as for that which indicates the second category, what was narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Qasim ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Sayqal, who said: He wrote to him, 'O my master, a man vowed to fast every Friday permanently as long as he lives. That day coincided with Eid al-Fitr or Eid al-Adha, or the days of Tashriq, or he traveled, or he became ill. Is he obligated to fast that day or make it up, or what should he do, O my master?' So he wrote to him, 'Allah has relieved you of fasting on all these days, and you fast one day in place of one day, if Allah wills, the Exalted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed voluntary fasts for a person who traveled or was ill?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *nadr* (voluntary vow) and *sunnah* fasts, establishing that missed voluntary fasts do not carry the strict compensatory weight of obligatory ones. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on consistency (*dawam*) in worship, encouraging the believer to maintain the practice of the three monthly days even if not strictly required to make them up. The ruling also demonstrates the flexibility of divine law, where exemptions for travel or illness are granted without burdening the individual with redundant makeup fasts.
